summary: Devil Mountain tower in San Juan NF, Colorado, built 1955; moved to New Mexico in 1996 as the Atole lookout, leaving only radio-tower footings on the peak.

facts.status_note: Tower moved to New Mexico in 1996; only the footings remain on Devil Mountain, used for a radio tower

events.note: 30-ft steel tower with 13x13 ft cab, built to take over lookout duties from Chimney Rock; NHLR says the Forest Service constructed it as Devil Mountain Lookout

Declared surplus in the 1990s. The Colorado register says it was sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation; the New Mexico register says the BIA claimed it. In 1996 a Chinook helicopter moved it in three trips to Tecolote Mesa, NM, where it is called Atole

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Colorado register gives 30 feet and a 13-foot cab for the Devil Mountain tower. The New Mexico register gives 40 feet and a 14-foot cab for the same structure at Atole. Neither explains the difference, so the story reports both.
The Colorado register says the tower was sold to the Jicarilla Apache Nation. The New Mexico register says the Bureau of Indian Affairs claimed it. The story reports both without choosing.

notes_for_editor: No source I read describes staffing, fires, current access or the site's condition beyond the footings, so the story leaves those out and the facts carry no access entry. The register's 30-foot figure is converted to 9.1 m for height_m. Coordinates: the brief's point (37.28419, -107.27622) matches the Colorado register; firelookout.org lists 37.28442, -107.27596, about 35 m away, the same site. The brief's elevation (3,027.3 m) matches the register. One web search was run. A core.tdar.org record titled Devil Mountain Fire Lookout (a 1996 assessment of Colorado national forest properties) appeared in results but was not opened; it may hold construction detail.
